tip: 'umarım' (I hope) is followed by the -ir general present here: 'iyileşirsin' (iyileş + ir + sin) = you get better.
'rağmen' (despite) needs the -a/-e ending on the noun: 'başarısızlığa' = 'başarısızlık' (k softens to ğ) + a = despite failure.
-alım means let's: 'başlayalım' (başla + yalım) = let's start, the we-form suggestion ending.
'göre' means according to and takes the -a/-e (to) ending: 'bana göre' = in my opinion; 'bana' is the -a form of 'ben' (I/me).
'-mış olmalı' means must have or probably has: 'bitmiş olmalı' = the battery must have died, a guess from evidence.
-ip links verbs sharing one subject; only the last carries tense: 'oturup dinlenmek' = to sit and rest.
For an action still going, put -dır on the time span plus present tense: 'yıllardır' ... 'yaşıyorum' = I have lived here for years.
-di is what you saw, -miş what you only heard: 'oynadı' = performed (seen), 'alkışlamış' = apparently applauded (reported).
'yürüyerek' means by walking. Add -erek or -arak to a verb stem to say how an action is done: 'yürü' plus -yerek.
'döndüğümde' means when I returned. The -düğümde ending turns a verb into a when I did X time clause.
'kalksaydım' means if I had gotten up. The -saydım ending marks a past condition that did not actually happen.
'kırmızıdan daha ucuz' means cheaper than the red. Mark the compared thing with -dan and add 'daha' before the adjective.
'olsa' means if I had. Plain -sa, not -saydı, states a present unreal wish, paired with 'isterdim' (I would want).
'giderdik' means we used to go. The -erdik ending describes a repeated habit in the past, not a single event.
'eğer' means if, but it is optional. The -sa on 'olursa' already carries the condition, so 'eğer' just reinforces it.
'binip' means get on and. The -ip ending links two verbs sharing one subject; only the last, 'giderim', takes the tense.
'biriktirirsem' means if I save. The -sem here sets a real future condition, so the main verb is future, 'gideceğim'.
'okula başladı' means started school. 'başlamak' takes the -a/-e (to) ending, so it attaches -a to 'okul', literally started to school.
'yazan' means who wrote. Add -an or -en to a verb when the noun after it did the action: 'yaz' plus -an describes 'yazar'.
'yaptığı' means that she makes. Use -tığı, not -an, when someone else is the doer: 'annem' makes the 'börek'.
'mi' marks what is being asked about. Placed after 'evde' and 'dışarı', with 'yoksa' between, it offers an either-or choice.
'rağmen' means despite. The noun before it takes the -a/-e (to) ending, so it is 'yağmura', not 'yağmur'.
'yağacakmış' means it will apparently snow. Adding -mış to the future -acak marks news you heard, not witnessed.
'haberlere göre' means according to the news. 'göre' takes the -a/-e (to) ending, so it is 'haberler' plus -e.
'alalım' means let's buy. The -alım ending on a verb makes a we-form suggestion, let's do it.
'gençken' means when he was young. Attach -ken to a word to mean while or when that state held.
Month names and proper nouns take an apostrophe before a suffix: 'Haziran'da' (Haziran + da = in June).
For half past, say the hour then 'buçuk': 'iki buçukta' = at two and a half, meaning half past two.
The verb 'alışmak' takes the -a/-e (to) ending: 'havaya alıştı' = got used to the weather, 'hava' plus ya.
'meğer' flags a fact you just realized and pairs with the -miş past: 'gitmişiz' = turns out we went.
